fields.Back: A description of the database, but NOT the data itself; similar to a type in a programming language.
An occurrence of a data item described in the schema, e.g. patient name 'Homer Simpson' with OHIP number '123-345-567'.
The data in the database at a moment in time: the current set of instances. Every add, delete or change of a value changes the state.

fields.Text: The schema of the schema is called {{c1::meta-data}}; the DBMS stores it for each database.
Defining a new database specifies its {{c1::schema}}; the initial state/snapshot is {{c2::empty}}.

fields.Front: Which changes frequently: the database schema, the database state, or both?
fields.Back: The state changes constantly (every insert/delete/update); the schema changes rarely.

fields.Text: Making sure every database state is a valid state is part of the job of the {{c1::DBMS}}.

fields.Front: Give the three-table example schema from the slides.
fields.Back: Patient (patient name, OHIP number); Room (room number, num of beds); Nurse (nurse name, nurse employee id).

fields.Front: What programming analogy does the instructor use for a schema?
fields.Back: Declaring a variable as integer, real or char tells you its type, not the number or letter it holds; the schema is like the type, describing the database but not the data.

fields.Front: Name three operations on the hospital database that the instructor says change the state (snapshot).
fields.Back: Deleting Homer; changing his OHIP number; changing the room he is in.

fields.Front: Give the instructor's two examples of the DBMS refusing to move to an invalid state.
fields.Back: Typing letters into an OHIP number that accepts only integers; inserting a new patient with a blank OHIP number ('every patient has to have an OHIP number').

fields.Front: What is the instructor's example of meta-data, and why does a DBMS hold a lot of it?
fields.Back: A description saying the hospital database has five tables. The DBMS stores such a schema-of-the-schema for every database it manages.

fields.Text: At creation you specify the {{c1::schema}}; no data has been stored, so 'you can have a schema with an {{c2::empty}} database'.
